notes.L1:
Before you start, look at Pigment CI on the branch (`gh run list --branch claude/pigment-photocraft -L 4` works here). If the newest finished run is red, find out why and fix that first, in its own commit; if it is still running, go on and look again later. The generative AI port (P1 to P5, its reviews and a final check) is complete on the branch; docs/generative-ai.md and docs/FORK.md describe it.

Three things the spec does not say:
1. **The CI smoke test knows the old behaviour.** `.github/workflows/pigment-ci.yml`, step "CLI smoke test", writes a minimal Pigment 0.4 ZIP (document.json and a layers/1.png that is only a PNG signature) and requires `pigment-cli info` to fail with "This file was saved by Pigment 0.4 or earlier. Opening these files is coming in a later update." Change that part in the same commit in which legacy files start to open, or CI goes red: a damaged legacy file must still fail with the typed error and its new message, and one of your committed fixtures must convert to PNG with pigment-cli. Keep the step's comment and the header comment of the workflow true. Other places quote that message too (grep the repository for "coming in a later update": tests, docs/FORK.md, README.md, docs/RELEASE-NOTES-0.5.0.md, the i18n catalogue if it has a row).
2. **The fixtures need the real JavaScript writer.** The JavaScript app is on the local branch claude/fervent-newton-263lz3 (`git worktree add <a folder in the scratchpad> claude/fervent-newton-263lz3`, not inside /home/user/claude/pigment). node and npm work here (the npm registry is reachable); release downloads from github.com are blocked by the proxy, so a native module that fetches a prebuilt binary from GitHub may have to build from source or be avoided (the JavaScript unit tests under pigment/tests/unit show what already runs under node without a browser). Remove the worktree when you are done; commit only the fixtures, the generator script and its README.
3. **README.md and docs/RELEASE-NOTES-0.5.0.md** say old .pigment files do not open yet. Say there what opens after your package and what still waits for the next two (adjustments, fills, shapes and styles in L2; text, smart objects and filters in L3), so the text is true at every commit.

When your work is pushed and your notes are written, return: don't wait for CI on your last push. The next engineer checks it first.
